title: Sungic (Shelter Island)
summary: Sungic is a point of land and creek on the east side of Shelter Island, facing Gardiners Bay.
history_content: The name was preserved on local maps and in local usage rather than in early deeds. It is connected with the rocky shoreline and a nearby Rocky Point.
translation_content:
Sungic is interpreted as a stony place, compared with related words for stone and with the Sunwicks entry.

Why Place Names Matter

“Beyond the map's names are thousands upon thousands more, an ever growing and expanding atlas of intimate, geographical knowledge and experience.”

— Margaret Wickens Pearce, Coming Home to Indigenous Place Names in Canada (2017), map project description
preservation_content: Sungic preserves a local Shelter Island shoreline name tied to stone, creek, point, and map memory.
